R6F-grouse-drive-0003.name: 1.2 km N of Wynkes Creek
R6F-grouse-drive-0003.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
10 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
18 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 6 table (pages 50 and 51), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis).

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 62 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Tibbets Creek Rd, Hwy 16, Hwy 35, Brown Rd.
Park: 53.91985, -126.0699, pull off on Verdun (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk or drive slowly: the Verdun stretch, 5.1 km one way. About 101 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-4, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
R6F-grouse-drive-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-4: about 7,565 hunter days a year for all big game (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.83 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
